grammar_concept.title: Zero Conditional
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'If + present simple, ... present simple' to talk about things that are always true — general facts, scientific truths, or personal habits. Both parts of the sentence stay in the present simple.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: The Zero Conditional describes something that always happens under a certain condition — not a prediction about a specific future situation (that's the First Conditional), but a rule that is always true.
grammar_concept.example: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. If I drink coffee at night, I don't sleep well.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Se aqueces a água a 100°C, ela ferve. Se bebo café à noite, não durmo bem.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a misturar o Zero Conditional com o First Conditional, usando "will" na oração principal mesmo quando o significado é uma verdade geral ou um hábito ("If you heat water, it will boil" em vez de "it boils") — no Zero Conditional, as duas orações ficam sempre no Presente Simples, nunca com "will".
grammar_concept.correction: Nas duas orações do Zero Conditional (a condição e o resultado), use sempre o Presente Simples — nunca "will" — porque se está a falar de algo sempre verdadeiro, não de uma previsão sobre um caso específico no futuro.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Giving instructions: "If the light turns red, you stop the car."

vocabulary.definition_en: to reach the temperature at which a liquid turns into gas
example_sentences: Water boils at 100°C at sea level.

vocabulary.definition_en: to become solid because of very low temperature
to change and become something different
example_sentences: If you heat water enough, it turns into steam.

exercises.prompt: Complete: If you heat ice, it ___ (melt).
exercises.explanation: No Zero Conditional, a oração de resultado fica no Presente Simples: "melts", não "will melt".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "will melt" (como no First Conditional) é o erro mais comum aqui.

exercises.prompt: Complete: If I ___ (drink) coffee at night, I don't sleep well.
exercises.explanation: A oração da condição também fica no Presente Simples: "drink", não "will drink".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Tentar usar "will" na oração da condição é um erro comum, por confusão com o First Conditional.

correct_answer: to become solid because of very low temperature
distractors: to become liquid because of heat
to become gas because of heat
exercises.explanation: "Freeze" é o oposto de "boil" — descreve o líquido a tornar-se sólido, não gás.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. At what temperature does water freeze?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "If the temperature drops to zero degrees, water freezes."
exercises.transcript: Water is a simple example of the zero conditional. If you heat water to 100 degrees, it boils. If the temperature drops to zero degrees, water freezes.

exercises.prompt: Read: "If you mix blue and yellow paint, you get green. If you mix red and white, you get pink." What do you get if you mix blue and yellow?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente "you get green".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Se aqueces o gelo, ele derrete."
correct_answer: If you heat ice, it melts.
If you heat the ice, it melts.
exercises.explanation: Verdade geral: as duas orações ficam no Presente Simples — "heat" e "melts", nunca "will melt".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir para "it will melt" é o erro mais comum, por confusão com o First Conditional.

steps.content: In natural speech, "if you" often links together as /ɪˈfjuː/ — the "f" and "y" sounds blend, instead of being said as two separate, clearly-divided words.

steps.prompt: Say 2-3 sentences about things that are always true for you — a habit, or something that always happens under a certain condition.
Write 3 Zero Conditional sentences: one about science, one about a personal habit, and one giving an instruction.
